items.body:
## Summary

On the Windows desktop app, Browser Use rejects an exact HTTPS origin as blocked by a saved user permission even though the user-supplied Agent permissions screen shows **Always allow** for both default navigation and the matching site exception. The rejection persists after restarting Codex and establishing a fresh connection to the same Chrome profile.

The user explicitly requested submission of this diagnostic. This public report omits the website identity, account email, chat identifiers, local paths, screenshots, session transcripts, and private website data. The affected origin below is redacted.

## Environment

- Windows 11 Home, version 10.0.26200, 64-bit (read from OS metadata).
- Installed Windows app package: `OpenAI.Codex`, version `26.930.3930.0` (read via Windows package metadata; not an About-dialog version).
- Browser surface: Google Chrome extension connection, not the built-in browser.
- Tool: `mcp__cua_repl`.
- Observed: October 3, 2026, Europe/Madrid.
- Chrome/extension version and subscription: not collected.

## Observed reproduction

1. The user opens Settings > Computer Use > Chrome > Agent permissions.
2. Their screenshot shows Navigation and Downloads set to **Always allow** for both Default and the exact site entry.
3. The agent uses the documented API to create a new tab and navigate to the existing WordPress editor on that HTTPS origin (no `www`, no explicit port).
4. Browser Use rejects the call before the page loads, with the error below.
5. The user restarts Codex. The old browser connection becomes unavailable, and a new connection to the same Chrome profile is selected.
6. Repeating the same documented new-tab navigation through the fresh connection returns the identical denial.
7. The same connection successfully opens `https://help.openai.com`, so browser access is not universally unavailable.

Retained minimal timestamps:
- `2026-10-03T11:11:45.306Z`: new-tab navigation rejected.
- `2026-10-03T11:23:12.659Z`: new-tab navigation rejected again after the Codex restart/fresh browser connection.

## Actual error

Host redacted; the remaining error text is verbatim:

```text
Browser Use rejected this action due to browser security policy.
Reason: A saved user permission setting blocks this action.
Browser use cannot access https://[redacted-origin] because the user has a saved preference that blocks it.
```

The tool prohibits workarounds and policy circumvention. We respected that restriction: no alternate browser surface, raw browser protocol, direct request to the blocked website, or permission-file mutation was used.

## Expected behavior

An explicit origin-level navigation allowance should be reflected in the effective permission decision, unless an overriding restriction applies. If a legitimate higher-priority restriction is responsible, the UI/error should identify its source and the supported recovery path instead of attributing the decision to a saved user block that contradicts the visible settings.

Please investigate the permission-source/UI mismatch and provide a supported recovery procedure. Stale state, another policy, and a product defect remain hypotheses; this report does not establish the cause.

## Diagnostics and reporting limitation

- Read-only inspection found no matching `browser_use` deny/default/origin policy in the personal `config.toml`; the workspace's `.codex/config.toml` does not exist.
- The inspected computer-use configuration files did not expose an explicit navigation/origin deny for this site. This is not an exhaustive audit of cloud/device policy.
- The Help Center chat received the diagnosis and contact email, but its AI explicitly said it cannot transfer this conversation to a person or issue a case number, and directed us to GitHub.
- No in-app `/feedback` submission receipt was generated: the agent lacks a tool to operate the application's own message composer, and the user is currently remote on mobile.
- No private transcript, credentials, cookies, account identifiers, or website/student data are attached.

Related symptoms, without claiming the same root cause: #43754 (Chrome extension on macOS) and #37738 (allow UI vs saved-permission denial).

## Read-only follow-up: matching deny in the current chat session

The bot's potential-duplicate list led us to the read-only diagnostic suggestion in [#49453](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/49453#issuecomment-5917957249). We inspected a different configuration layer from the files described above and found:

- `%USERPROFILE%/.codex/browser/sessions/[current-chat].toml` exists.
- Its `[origins]` / `denied` list contains the exact affected HTTPS origin (website identity redacted). The real session identifier and other origin values are omitted.
- The general browser configuration at `%USERPROFILE%/.codex/browser/config.toml` contains `approval_mode = "never_ask"` and `download_approval_mode = "never_ask"`. The user-supplied permissions screenshot shows **Always allow** for navigation and downloads, including the affected site's exception.
- The session file's last-modified timestamp predates the general browser configuration's last modification. This is a timestamp observation only; it does not identify which component wrote the deny or establish the effective precedence.

This is concrete evidence of a matching per-chat deny while the visible general settings allow the site, consistent with the saved-permission rejection. It does not prove a code-level root cause or identify the creator of the deny.

No policy files were changed, no alternate access or bypass was attempted, and access has not been restored. The earlier negative configuration checks were limited to the personal/workspace config and computer-use files; they did not include this session file.

The official Chrome extension troubleshooting documentation covers the general Manage allow/block list and new-chat recovery for connection state. We did not find a documented mechanism that specifically revokes this per-session denial. Please clarify the intended precedence and provide a supported UI recovery path that reconciles this session rule with the user's **Always allow** choice.

We have kept this issue open: the automated duplicate suggestions (#50191, #50240, #49453) establish related symptoms, not a confirmed shared root cause or a verified fix.

items.title: macOS: Computer Use MCP helpers remain resident across long-lived Codex conversations (~903 MiB RSS)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: mcp
labels.description: Issues related to the use of model context protocol (MCP) servers

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
## Summary

Computer Use MCP helper processes remain resident for hours or days across multiple long-lived Codex conversations on macOS, with a noticeable combined memory and CPU cost. I frequently finish a task that used Computer Use and find the helpers still running afterward.

This report includes observations from the current desktop app and `codex-cli 0.160.0` daemon. It is a suspected lifecycle / idle-resource-retention issue, not a confirmed unbounded leak: several conversations are open concurrently, and I have not mapped each helper to an active or completed conversation.

## Environment

- macOS 26.5.1, arm64.
- ChatGPT desktop app: 26.928.20755, build 12246 (bundle identifier `com.openai.codex`).
- Background app-server daemon: `codex-cli 0.160.0`.
- Desktop-bundled CLI: `codex-cli 0.159.0`.
- Computer Use app: 26.924.1001281, build 1001281.
- Multiple Codex conversations open concurrently.

## Observed behavior

Two process snapshots on October 3, 2026:

| Snapshot | Live helpers | Combined RSS | Sum of sampled CPU percentages |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Initial investigation | 32 | 996.5 MiB | 17.0% |
| Follow-up at 13:43 UTC | 31 | 903.4 MiB | 14.9% |

All helpers in both snapshots were `SkyComputerUseClient mcp`, rather than `turn-ended` notifier invocations.

In the follow-up snapshot:

| Parent | Helper count |
| --- | ---: |
| Background Codex app-server daemon (`0.160.0`) | 25 |
| Main desktop-bundled Codex process (`0.159.0`) | 5 |
| Another desktop-bundled Codex process | 1 |

Some helpers had been running for approximately 41 hours. Individual helpers typically held about 29–33 MiB RSS and reported approximately 0.3–0.6% CPU in that snapshot. The helpers were still children of their Codex parent processes; these were not PID-1 orphans.

The count fell from 32 to 31 between snapshots, and combined RSS also fell. Therefore these measurements establish prolonged retention and resource cost, but do not establish monotonic growth or prove that every retained helper is stale. No processes were killed during this investigation.

## Workflow to investigate / reproduce

1. On macOS, enable the bundled Computer Use integration.
2. Keep several Codex conversations open and perform ordinary coding tasks, including occasional browser or desktop verification.
3. Let tasks finish and leave the conversations open.
4. Inspect helper count, parentage, age and resident memory:

```sh
ps -axo pid,ppid,etime,%cpu,rss,comm \
  | awk 'NR == 1 || /\/SkyComputerUseClient$/'
```

`rss` is in KiB on macOS. This command prints executable paths rather than full arguments, avoiding any turn metadata in command-line payloads.

These steps describe the workflow in which the problem was observed. I have not yet isolated a clean, single-conversation reproduction or tested whether closing all conversations tears down every helper.

## Expected behavior / requested investigation

Please clarify the intended lifetime and ownership of `SkyComputerUseClient mcp` helpers. If a helper belongs to an idle or completed conversation, reuse or release it as appropriate so retained resource usage stays bounded. If one resident helper per open conversation is intentional, please clarify that behavior and investigate whether idle helpers need to keep consuming measurable CPU.

## Related reports

- #43471: idle desktop app-server accumulating MCP helper processes.
- #47580: interactive CLI sessions accumulating helpers across turns.
- #29157: leaked `turn-ended` notifier helpers; a different invocation mode from this report.

This is a current-version report with process snapshots and an explicit distinction between observed retention and an unproven leak. I cannot yet confirm whether it shares the root cause of those reports.

items.title: MCP aggregate resource inventory drops internal errors from resource-supporting servers

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: mcp
labels.description: Issues related to the use of model context protocol (MCP) servers

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: tool-calls
labels.description: Issues related to tool calling

items.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

Reproduced with current stable `codex-cli 0.160.0`, previous stable `0.159.3`, and
`0.162.0-alpha.10`. Current main source checked separately at
`b741e480e203f037ca726bc2a76d99a8e8668e66`; I did not build main.

### What subscription do you have?

Not applicable: the reproduction uses a loopback scripted Responses endpoint;
no OpenAI API key, subscription, or real model inference is required.

### Which model were you using?

No model inference. The custom local provider accepts the `gpt-5.2` slug and
replays a single advertised inventory tool call to isolate the client path.
This is a deterministic harness/tool failure, not a model reliability result.

### What platform is your computer?

Windows x64, NT build `10.0.26200`; also verified on Linux x86_64 under WSL2
(`6.18.40.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2`). Platform and binary hashes are recorded.
Safe runtime metadata was captured on the same hosts after the confirmatory
matrix; it is linked with the evidence and is not asserted per run.

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

Non-interactive subprocess pipes; no terminal emulator or multiplexer involved.
Python 3.12.3 on WSL; Python 3.11.5 on Windows.

### Codex doctor report

Not collected: this reproduction bypasses user config with CLI-only overrides,
requires no auth, successfully initializes its synthetic MCP server, and records
fixture-side protocol counters. Full host diagnostics are unnecessary for this
isolated error-propagation path.

### What issue are you seeing?

`list_mcp_resources({})` and `list_mcp_resource_templates({})` omit a server's
inventory error and return an unqualified successful empty/partial catalog.
The affected server initializes successfully and explicitly advertises
`capabilities.resources: {}`. It returns a valid JSON-RPC internal error
`-32603` to the inventory request, not an unsupported optional method.

Observed aggregate model-facing output:

```json
{"resources":[]}
```

The corresponding `exec --json` MCP tool item has `status: "completed"` and
`error: null`. Windows stderr contains the inventory warning, but that error
does not appear in the tool output sent to the next model request. The WSL
stderr flag was false; other WSL log channels were not inspected. A genuinely healthy empty
server returns the same inventory text. With one healthy and one failing server,
the successful resource is retained but the failed server disappears without
partialness/error metadata.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Download public Codex stable `0.160.0` for your platform.
2. Obtain the pinned minimal fixture and replay harness linked under Evidence.
3. From the research repository, using Python 3.10+:

```sh
python -m harness.replay --codex /path/to/codex --condition error_aggregate
python -m harness.replay --codex /path/to/codex --condition error_named
```

The harness starts a loopback Responses-compatible endpoint and the actual
stdio MCP subprocess. The replay asks Codex to call an advertised inventory
tool, records only its model-facing output, and stops. The fixture independently
records successful initialization and `resources/list -> -32603`. It contains
no real backend or adversarial prompt and preserves credential stores/config.

Only the named control's tool arguments change from `{}` to
`{"server":"probe"}`. That control returns the original error and
`status: "failed"`. `mixed_aggregate`, `empty_aggregate`,
`template_error_aggregate`, and `template_error_named` exercise the relevant
ablations. `invalid_aggregate` is an additional, separately identified malformed
payload check; it is not needed for the valid-error reproduction.

### What is the expected behavior?

Preserve the failure of a resource-supporting server in the model-facing
inventory result. Best-effort aggregation can retain healthy resources while
identifying unavailable servers or marking the inventory partial. A complete
empty inventory must remain distinguishable from a failed query.

**Proposed invariant / expected behavior:** a declared-resource server's inventory error must not
become an unqualified successful empty/partial catalog.
This is an error-provenance request, not a claim that an official contract
requires atomic failure. Best-effort preservation of healthy results is useful.

### Additional information

#### Reproduction rate and controls

Windows results below are **failed invariant / valid software executions**;
they are not rates of spontaneous model behavior. Each cell is repeated
independently in a fresh ephemeral exec invocation, with pilots excluded.

| Condition | 0.160.0 | 0.159.3 | 0.162.0-alpha.10 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Valid `-32603`, aggregate resources | 10/10 | 10/10 | 10/10 |
| Same error, named server | 0/10 | 0/10 | 0/10 |
| Healthy resource, aggregate | 0/10 | 0/10 | 0/10 |
| Healthy empty catalog, aggregate | 0/10 | 0/10 | 0/10 |
| One failing + one healthy server | 10/10 | 10/10 | 10/10 |
| Valid `-32603`, aggregate templates | 10/10 | 10/10 | 10/10 |
| Same template error, named server | 0/10 | 0/10 | 0/10 |

The named error passes the **error-visibility invariant**, not resource retrieval.
The generated full table includes durations, tool counts, malformed-payload
ablation, WSL replication, and all execution exclusions.

There were 240 valid Windows executions (eight conditions × ten repetitions ×
three versions) and 24 valid WSL stable executions (eight × three), with zero
execution exclusions. WSL reproduced aggregate resource/template and mixed
failures in 3/3 each; named, healthy, and genuine-empty controls violated the
invariant in 0/3 each. These counts are software reproduction checks, not
estimates of stochastic agent failure or real-world prevalence.

#### Evidence

Public evidence pinned to commit `2b99ab0ac6662b5b294dc50d68ec643d21bd3cc8`:

- [Minimal fixture](https://github.com/beibeihk/codex-failure-research/blob/2b99ab0ac6662b5b294dc50d68ec643d21bd3cc8/fixtures/mcp_inventory/server.py)
- [Replay harness](https://github.com/beibeihk/codex-failure-research/blob/2b99ab0ac6662b5b294dc50d68ec643d21bd3cc8/harness/replay.py)
- [Standalone instructions](https://github.com/beibeihk/codex-failure-research/blob/2b99ab0ac6662b5b294dc50d68ec643d21bd3cc8/docs/minimal-reproduction.md)
- [Windows records (240)](https://github.com/beibeihk/codex-failure-research/blob/2b99ab0ac6662b5b294dc50d68ec643d21bd3cc8/results/confirmatory-windows.jsonl)
- [WSL records (24)](https://github.com/beibeihk/codex-failure-research/blob/2b99ab0ac6662b5b294dc50d68ec643d21bd3cc8/results/confirmatory-wsl.jsonl)
- [Generated results and controls](https://github.com/beibeihk/codex-failure-research/blob/2b99ab0ac6662b5b294dc50d68ec643d21bd3cc8/reports/mcp-inventory-results.md)
- [Duplicate/current-source audit](https://github.com/beibeihk/codex-failure-research/blob/2b99ab0ac6662b5b294dc50d68ec643d21bd3cc8/research/duplicate-audit.md)
- [Technical report](https://github.com/beibeihk/codex-failure-research/blob/2b99ab0ac6662b5b294dc50d68ec643d21bd3cc8/docs/technical-report.md)
- [Safe post-run runtime metadata](https://github.com/beibeihk/codex-failure-research/blob/2b99ab0ac6662b5b294dc50d68ec643d21bd3cc8/research/runtime-metadata.json)
- [Independent adversarial review and final acceptance](https://github.com/beibeihk/codex-failure-research/blob/2b99ab0ac6662b5b294dc50d68ec643d21bd3cc8/reports/independent-review.md)
- [Verifier](https://github.com/beibeihk/codex-failure-research/blob/2b99ab0ac6662b5b294dc50d68ec643d21bd3cc8/analyzers/invariants.py)
- [Predeclared scenario](https://github.com/beibeihk/codex-failure-research/blob/2b99ab0ac6662b5b294dc50d68ec643d21bd3cc8/scenarios/mcp_inventory.json)

#### Source mechanism and design hypothesis

High confidence in the observed mechanism: aggregate resource/template calls
reach [`collect_resource_results`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/b741e480e203f037ca726bc2a76d99a8e8668e66/codex-rs/codex-mcp/src/binding_clients.rs#L137-L156). Its error
branch logs a warning without preserving the server error in its returned map.
The [core resource handler](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/b741e480e203f037ca726bc2a76d99a8e8668e66/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/mcp_resource.rs#L351-L370) serializes that map with a success flag. Named calls
instead propagate their `Result` error. The same path remains in inspected main.

Preserving per-server failures alongside healthy catalogs is a possible design
direction, not a validated patch. I have not demonstrated downstream model-task
harm or measured real backend-outage prevalence. No model change is proposed.

#### Related reports checked

#6217 already records aggregate emptiness versus a named `-32601` error, so
this symptom and possibly the error-dropping mechanism are not claimed as new.
#11264, #14242 and #6215 concern tools-only servers and empty-resource
interpretation; #37468 concerns `-32601` and optional capability probing;
#25061 concerns a non-returning resource probe. This reproduction instead uses
a successfully initialized, resource-advertising server and an immediate valid
internal error. Happy-path results remain available; failure provenance is lost.
The contribution is stronger evidence under this declared-resource/internal-error
condition. I found no report with this complete predicate in the recorded searches, but
will defer to maintainers if an existing canonical issue should receive the evidence.

An owner-approved unattended workflow cannot reliably send steering instructions between its desktop tasks. Requiring the owner to copy every message manually defeats the workflow.

## Observations, not claimed root causes
1. An existing desktop sender task no longer exposes native task send/read/list/create tools. Rechecking after an app update, macOS update, restart and user-reported hooks reload did not restore them in that task.
2. A fresh, strictly read-only task on the same Mac exposed those native tools at 13:22 UTC on 3 October. It checked availability only. It did not invoke them or replace the sender.

4. A subsequent request to prepare an inactive correction, test synthetic fixtures and obtain review was rejected despite explicit owner approval being relayed. 5. Changing the UI preference from Queue to Steer did not establish that every programmatic sending route follows that preference. One disposable test previously demonstrated in-turn receipt; this did not resolve later tool loss or approval rejection.

## Expected
Native tool availability should remain coherent across supported task lifecycles, or the app should provide an explicit supported refresh/recovery mechanism. labels.name: bug

labels.name: app

items.body:
### Version and environment

- Managed app-server daemon: `codex-cli 0.160.0` (latest stable release when checked).
- Ubuntu on WSL2, `Linux 6.6.114.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2`, x86_64.
- Windows Codex Desktop package version: `26.928.2636.0`.
- Desktop connects locally to the WSL backend through SSH / `app-server proxy`; the phone uses the WSL backend's remote-control connection.
- Signed in with ChatGPT; subscription tier not provided. Model is not relevant to this lifecycle reproduction.
- Commands were launched from Windows PowerShell through `wsl.exe`. A full doctor bundle is not attached; targeted observations are below.

### Problem

Enabling remote control through the durable `remoteControl/enable` RPC (`params: null`) successfully persists the app-server's enable preference and connects it. However, if the managed daemon's separate startup preference is off, restarting that daemon leaves remote control `disabled`.

Desktop's local WSL connection recovers while the phone's WSL remote endpoint remains unavailable. Setting the daemon startup preference through `remote-control start --json` fixes the restart behavior on the same binary and network.

### Reproduction

These steps intentionally restart the tested WSL daemon and can interrupt its active tasks. Use the actual managed daemon executable, rather than an npm CLI that might be a different version:

```bash
CODEX="$HOME/.codex/packages/app-server-daemon/current/bin/codex"
"$CODEX" --version
"$CODEX" app-server daemon disable-remote-control
```

The explicit disable establishes the reproduction precondition; it is not evidence that the user manually disabled remote access before the original incidents.

Connect a client to the running managed daemon's Unix WebSocket listener, initialize it, and issue:

```json
{"id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"clientInfo":{"name":"codex_remote_repro","version":"1.0"},"capabilities":{"experimentalApi":true}}}
{"method":"initialized"}
{"id":2,"method":"remoteControl/enable","params":null}
{"id":3,"method":"remoteControl/status/read","params":null}
```

The transport is WebSocket over the Unix listener, not raw newline-delimited JSON written to a control socket. Poll status until `connected`. This is the same enable method/parameter shape observed in the installed Desktop client; the controlled test sent it directly.

The daemon PID remains unchanged and its command line still lacks `--remote-control`. The enable log includes:

```text
effective_persistence_preference=Some(true)
```

Then run:

```bash
"$CODEX" app-server daemon restart
```

Reconnect and initialize the probe against the new daemon. `remoteControl/status/read` returns `disabled` with `environmentId: null`. It remains disabled after 30 seconds, even though Desktop's local WSL connection has reconnected by then.

For the control case:

```bash
"$CODEX" remote-control start --json
# Wait for remoteControl/status/read to report connected.
"$CODEX" app-server daemon restart
```

The new daemon has `--remote-control`; status goes from `connecting` to `connected` automatically, in approximately seven seconds in this run, and remains connected at the later check.

### Observed comparison

| Action | Daemon startup flag | Remote state |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Durable RPC enable with startup preference off | No `--remote-control`; same PID | `connected`; persisted preference logged as `Some(true)` |
| Restart after that RPC | No `--remote-control`; new PID | `disabled`, still disabled after local Desktop reconnection |
| `remote-control start --json` | `--remote-control`; new PID | `connected` |
| Restart after CLI start | `--remote-control`; new PID | Automatically returns to `connected` |

The complete comparison used the same binary, network, and remote registration. No Windows Desktop/Windows Codex process was restarted, and WSL itself was not shut down.

### Source analysis

The release-pinned code appears to explain the observed behavior:

1. The managed daemon's [launch path](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.160.0/codex-rs/app-server-daemon/src/backend/pid.rs#L370) omits `--remote-control` and sets `REMOTE_CONTROL_DISABLED_ENV_VAR` when its startup preference is false.
2. The CLI [selects `DisabledEphemeral`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.160.0/codex-rs/cli/src/main.rs#L1246) in that case, rather than `ResolvePersisted`.
3. The RPC [processor](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.160.0/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/remote_control_processor.rs#L32) enables the transport; the [desired-state implementation](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.160.0/codex-rs/app-server-transport/src/transport/remote_control/desired_state.rs#L131) persists its preference. This does not synchronize the separate daemon startup setting.
4. In contrast, [`ensure_remote_control_started`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.160.0/codex-rs/app-server-daemon/src/lib.rs#L679) updates the daemon startup setting before starting/enabling the backend.

Thus the persisted app-server preference is not simply missing: a separate explicit startup-disable setting takes precedence on the next launch.

### Expected behavior and workaround

For remote access enabled durably through Desktop, a routine managed-daemon restart should preserve effective enablement. The integration may need to synchronize the daemon startup setting, or otherwise resolve precedence between these two persistence mechanisms. A regression test covering durable RPC enable followed by managed-daemon restart would help.

The tested workaround is `"$CODEX" remote-control start --json`. It can restart the WSL daemon when it changes the startup setting, even if the final JSON says `daemon.status: alreadyRunning`; that field alone does not establish that the entire command avoided a restart.

Rapid restarts also briefly produced `409 Remote app server already online`, which cleared automatically. That transient reconnect error is distinct from the persistent `disabled` state described here.

### Scope and related report

Related symptom report: #49436. I have not established that its author's incident has the same cause.

On this host, earlier outages coincided with managed-daemon replacement around upgrades. The controlled restart reproduction establishes the mechanism above, but no pre-incident settings snapshot exists and the historical upgrade itself was not replayed. I therefore cannot prove that every earlier outage had this cause or identify an introducing release.

items.title: Cloud reminder discovery: delegated local task exposes working _peek outside ALL_TOOLS

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

items.body:
### What issue are you seeing?

A delegated local task can directly call the advertised cloud-reminder read tool `mcp__codex_apps__automations._peek({})` successfully, while that same tool and the other directly advertised cloud-automation tools are absent from `functions.exec`'s `ALL_TOOLS` registry. Discovery based only on that registry can therefore incorrectly conclude that reminder readback is unavailable.

This was observed while investigating reminder-tool availability in a dot on October 2–3, 2026. The dot's reported registry exposed create/update/list/run and event-related automation tools, but no peek/read/get tool. **The dot's own direct-tool availability has not been established.** The confirmed working call was in the delegated local diagnostic task.

This concerns ChatGPT/dot cloud reminders under `mcp__codex_apps__automations`. Codex's separate local scheduling tool, `mcp__codex_app__automation_update`, is a different interface.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed diagnostic sequence on October 3, 2026, approximately 13:08 UTC:

1. From a dot, create/delegate a local diagnostic task authorized only to inspect the available automation tools and read existing reminder configuration.
2. Inspect both the task's directly advertised tools and its Code Mode registry. The task directly advertised:
   - `mcp__codex_apps__automations._peek`
   - `mcp__codex_apps__automations._list`
   - `mcp__codex_apps__automations._create`
   - `mcp__codex_apps__automations._update`
   - `mcp__codex_apps__automations._run_now`
   - `mcp__codex_apps__automations._list_event_sources`
   - `mcp__codex_apps__automations._discover_webhook_schema`
3. Inspect the registry inside `functions.exec`:

   ```js
   text(ALL_TOOLS
     .filter(t => t.name.startsWith("mcp__codex_apps__automations"))
     .map(t => t.name));
   ```

   The directly advertised cloud-automation tools above were absent from that registry.
4. Because `_peek` is directly advertised, invoke it through its direct tool surface, outside `functions.exec`:

   ```text
   mcp__codex_apps__automations._peek({})
   ```

5. Actual result: the call succeeded with `isError:false`. It returned the existing cloud automations and matched the two reminders being checked, including their schedules and enabled settings. Reminder IDs, prompts, and exact schedules are omitted here for privacy.

Only `_peek` was called in that diagnostic. No create/update/pause/delete/run operation or notification delivery was tested. A separate local task preparing this report also advertises these seven direct tools while the same registry filter returns `[]`; it did not repeat the reminder read.

### What is the expected behavior?

Tool discovery should let an agent determine the supported reminder capabilities without treating an empty Code Mode registry search as proof that no callable tool exists.

If direct and Code Mode tools intentionally use separate catalogs, the discovery guidance should clearly describe the scope of `ALL_TOOLS` and how to inspect both surfaces. If a capability is unavailable in a particular dot/task, a supported explanation or recovery path would help. Each dot should not have to rediscover this distinction independently.

### Current workaround

Create/delegate a **read-only local diagnostic task**, with authorization to read the relevant reminder configuration. In that task:

1. Inspect its **directly advertised tools in addition to `ALL_TOOLS`**.
2. If `mcp__codex_apps__automations._peek` is directly exposed, call that direct read-only tool.
3. Match the requested reminders and return only their target schedules and enabled settings to the parent.

This worked for configuration readback in the diagnostic described above. Reminder mutation and push/notification delivery remain untested. The workaround depends on the child actually exposing the tool; it is not established for every dot or independently opened local task. Do not guess undocumented APIs or bypass permissions.

### Additional information

Environment:
- Connected macOS desktop; dot-originated delegated local task.
- macOS 27.0.1, build 26A434.
- Installed desktop app bundle identifies itself as ChatGPT, version `26.930.21537`, build `12776`, bundle identifier `com.openai.codex`.
- Bundled Codex Framework version `154.0.8037.93` (framework metadata, not a verified Codex CLI version).
- App/framework versions were read from installed bundle metadata when preparing this report, rather than recorded during the earlier diagnostic.
- Diagnostic shell: zsh; task timezone: Etc/UTC; workspace-write sandbox with automatic approval review.

Scope and uncertainty:
- A working read call and the registry/direct-tool mismatch are confirmed in the delegated diagnostic.
- This does not prove why the dot's registry lacks a peek tool, that the dot cannot call a direct peek tool, that all dots are affected, or that the mismatch causes every reported reminder failure.
- No claim of a proven backend/root cause or failed reminder delivery is made.
- No settings changes, credential/secret reads, or undocumented API probes were used for the diagnostic.

Duplicate review:
- #30905 and #29128 concern missing/inconsistent exposure of the older local `automation_update` interface.
- #32294 concerns that local tool being advertised without a handler.
- #32101 concerns a missing ranked `tool_search` primitive while deferred tools remain reachable through `ALL_TOOLS`.
- #49729 concerns dot/local-project task creation and follow-up routing.

These are analogous or adjacent reports; none describes this observed cloud-reminder direct-call success with absence from `ALL_TOOLS`. Exact searches for `"_peek"` and `"mcp__codex_apps__automations"` found no existing issue. Filing under the repository's integration/Other Bug template.

Private task IDs, reminder contents, local paths, account details, and private instruction text are omitted.

items.body:
### What version of Codex desktop app is running?

OpenAI.Codex **26.930.2377.0** (MSIX, Windows Store package `OpenAI.Codex_2p2nqsd0c76g0`), Windows 11 x64.
Also present: codex CLI 0.158.0 (npm), app-server daemon 0.160.0.

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 11 (build 26300 x64). Git for Windows installed at `C:\Program Files\Git` (includes `mingw64\bin\connect.exe`). Local HTTP proxy (Clash) on `127.0.0.1:7890`.

### What issue are you seeing?

The **Recommended skills** tab fails to load with `git fetch failed`. The desktop app composes a git proxy-helper command in POSIX style and executes it via **PowerShell**, which fails on the very first token:

```
git fetch failed: exec : The term 'exec' is not recognized as the name of a cmdlet, function, script file, or operable program.
+ exec "C:/Program Files/Git/mingw64/bin/connect.exe" -H 127.0.0.1:7890 ...
    + CategoryInfo          : ObjectNotFound: (exec:String) [], CommandNotFoundException
    + FullyQualifiedErrorId : CommandNotFoundException
Connection closed by UNKNOWN port 65535
fatal: Could not read from remote repository. Please make sure you have the correct access rights and the repository exists.
```

(The Chinese-localized variant of the same PowerShell error is written to the desktop log as mojibake, because the GBK output is read back as UTF-8.)

### Root cause

The skills-recommended fetcher composes its git proxy-helper command in **POSIX shell style**:

```
exec "C:/Program Files/Git/mingw64/bin/connect.exe" -H 127.0.0.1:7890 <host> <port>
```

`exec` is a POSIX shell builtin prefix. On Windows the desktop runs this string through **PowerShell**, where `exec` does not exist → `CommandNotFoundException` → the connector never runs → ssh reports `Connection closed by UNKNOWN port 65535` → `git fetch` fails.

Notes:

- `connect.exe` (the HTTP-proxy connector shipped with Git for Windows) and the `-H 127.0.0.1:7890` argument are fine — the only fatal token is the POSIX `exec` prefix combined with the PowerShell execution path.
- The command string is composed internally by the desktop app. It does **not** come from any user configuration surface: we verified `git config` (global/system), `~/.ssh/config` (no `ProxyCommand`), environment variables, `~/.codex/config.toml` (all encodings), and the MSIX package data (`Settings.dat`, `LocalState`, `LocalCache`) — none contain `connect.exe`.

### Expected behavior

The proxy-helper child process should spawn without routing through an incompatible shell on Windows — e.g. drop the `exec` prefix on Windows, invoke `connect.exe` directly as an executable with `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`, or execute via `cmd.exe /c` instead of PowerShell.

### Impact

Only the **Recommended** tab of the skills page (discovery of new skills). Installed skills, local skills and all other functionality are unaffected.

### Additional notes

- The PowerShell error is localized (zh-CN, GBK) and is written into the desktop log read back as UTF-8, producing mojibake. Consider forcing UTF-8 or stripping ANSI/localized chunks when logging child-process stderr.
- Related Windows spawning issues in this build family: #48074 (terminal windows flash — daemon spawns console helpers without `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`), #48826 (hooks flashing, fixed by disabling hooks).
- Happy to provide full desktop logs (`LocalCache\Local\Codex\Logs\2026\10\02\…`) — they contain the complete failed command line and the GBK-mojibake PowerShell error.
